title: Who Is the Rich Man That Shall Be Saved? (Quis dives salvetur), esp. 42
author: Clement of Alexandria
summary: Homily on Mark 10:17-31 closing with the story of the aged apostle John, back from Patmos 'after the tyrant's death', reclaiming a young man who had become a robber chief. Quoted by Eusebius, Church History 3.23.

title: Commentary on the Apocalypse
author: Victorinus of Pettau
summary: The oldest surviving Latin commentary on Revelation; says John saw the visions while condemned to the mines of Patmos by Domitian (on 10:11) and identifies the king who 'is' in 17:10 with Domitian.

title: On Illustrious Men (De viris illustribus), esp. 9 on John
author: Jerome
summary: Catalogue of Christian writers; dates John's banishment to Patmos and the writing of the Apocalypse to the fourteenth year of Domitian and his return to Ephesus under Nerva.

title: Against Jovinian, esp. 1.26
author: Jerome
summary: Treatise on virginity and asceticism; in 1.26 it reports Tertullian's account of John being cast into boiling oil at Rome and attributes the act to Nero.

title: Prescription against Heretics, esp. 36
author: Tertullian
summary: Argues that the apostolic churches hold the true faith; chapter 36 lists Rome's glories, including John plunged unhurt into boiling oil and then sent to his island exile.

title: Apology, esp. 5
author: Tertullian
summary: Defence of Christians addressed to Roman governors; chapter 5 names Nero as the first persecutor and Domitian as 'a portion of Nero in cruelty' who soon stopped and recalled those he had banished.

title: Commentary on Matthew, esp. 16.6 (on Matthew 20:22-23)
author: Origen
summary: Origen's commentary on Matthew; on the cup of James and John he says 'the king of the Romans, as tradition teaches' condemned John to Patmos, without naming the emperor.

title: The Muratorian Fragment (Muratorian Canon)
author: Anonymous (Latin manuscript published by L. A. Muratori, 1740)
summary: Early list of New Testament books; says Paul, 'following the order of his predecessor John', wrote to seven churches by name, and that John in the Apocalypse writes to seven churches yet speaks to all.

title: Panarion (Medicine Chest against Heresies), esp. 51.12 and 51.33
author: Epiphanius of Salamis
summary: Catalogue and refutation of eighty heresies; in the section on the Alogi it twice places John's prophesying on Patmos in the time of Claudius Caesar.

title: Letter to the Philippians, esp. 11.3
author: Polycarp of Smyrna
summary: Letter of the bishop of Smyrna to the church at Philippi; 11.3 (extant in Latin) says Paul boasted of the Philippians in the churches 'which alone then knew the Lord, for we had not yet known him'.

title: 1 Clement (Letter of the Church at Rome to the Church at Corinth)
author: Clement of Rome (traditional)
summary: Letter from Rome urging the Corinthian church to restore its deposed elders; opens by apologising for delay caused by 'sudden and repeated misfortunes and calamities' (1.1).

title: Roman History, esp. 66.19 and 67.14
author: Cassius Dio
summary: Greek history of Rome; records a false Nero under Titus (66.19) and Domitian's execution of Flavius Clemens and exile of Flavia Domitilla in 95 on a charge of 'atheism' and drifting into Jewish ways (67.14).

title: Commentary on the Apocalypse
author: Arethas of Caesarea
summary: Byzantine Greek commentary on Revelation, reworking Andrew of Caesarea; applies parts of chapters 6-7 to the Jewish War.

title: The Date of John's Apocalypse: The Evidence of Some Roman Historians Reconsidered (New Testament Studies 25.1)
author: Albert A. Bell Jr.
summary: Classicist's argument from Roman historians' counting of emperors that Revelation 17:9-11 points to composition in 68-69, under Galba.

title: The Problem of the Domitianic Date of Revelation (New Testament Studies 39.4, 587-605)
author: J. Christian Wilson
summary: Questions the reliability of the Domitianic tradition and the evidence for Domitianic persecution, and argues for a date in the late 60s.

title: The Early Christians in Ephesus and the Date of Revelation, Again (Neotestamentica 39.1, 163-193)
author: Mark Wilson
summary: Reviews the arguments, especially from the history of the Ephesian church, and defends a date under Domitian.

title: Crisis and Catharsis: The Power of the Apocalypse
author: Adela Yarbro Collins
summary: Influential study of the social setting of Revelation; surveys the dating evidence and favours a date under Domitian, with John responding to a perceived rather than empire-wide crisis.

title: Revelation (Tyndale New Testament Commentaries)
author: Leon Morris
summary: Compact evangelical commentary; reviews the dating evidence and favours the Domitianic date.

title: A Commentary on the Apocalypse (2 vols.)
author: Moses Stuart
summary: Major nineteenth-century American commentary; argues at length for composition before the fall of Jerusalem, under Nero.

title: The Apocalypse of John
author: Charles Cutler Torrey
summary: Argues that Revelation was composed in Aramaic and dates it to the late 60s, before the temple's destruction.

title: Biblical Apocalyptics: A Study of the Most Notable Revelations of God and of Christ
author: Milton S. Terry
summary: Methodist scholar's study of biblical apocalyptic; dates Revelation before AD 70 and reads much of it in relation to the fall of Jerusalem.

title: The Apocalypse of St John I-III
author: F. J. A. Hort
summary: Posthumously published lectures with Greek text and notes on chapters 1-3; the introduction favours a date under Nero or just after.
